title: An alphabet in *gold*
hero_alt: All nineteen Yi Xing beads, pipes, links and spacers laid out in rows on teal suede
dek: Nineteen beads, pipes and links, each with a name. Every Yi Xing design is spelled from them.

body.html: Most jewellers name a bracelet after a season or a muse. We name ours after a bead. Every design in our collection is built from the same nineteen parts, cut in 916 gold, and each part has a name and a code you can ask for at the counter.

The beads carry most of the light. Lune is a moon-cut sphere of about 4 mm, faceted so it glints as it turns. Pavé is pineapple-cut, and Éclat, at about 8 mm, is the largest and brightest. Torsade is swirl-cut, Olive a fluted oval, Étoile a star-cut cushion cube and Grappe a cluster of fine gold grains. Halo, a rondelle edged with granules, frames the others.
The pipes set a design’s rhythm. Colonne is a fluted column, Fuseau a fluted spindle and Octave an eight-sided baton. Ligne is a slim polished tube about 16 mm long, and Spirale a coil.

Allongé, Anneau, Ciselé and Perlée join the parts, from an elongated paperclip link to a faceted ball barely more than a millimetre across. Disque and Couronne, a thin disc and a crown, sit between beads to give each one room.

body.text: Each design takes the name of its signature bead: Colonne for its pipes, Éclat for its spheres.

body.html: Because every design shares one alphabet, any bracelet can be lengthened, shortened or re-spelled. Bring yours to a boutique and we will add or remove parts to fit your wrist.
